text: Meanwhile, twenty one minutes before the train was due, six men were gathered at the bar of the Weary Gentleman saloon in Yellow Sky. <break time="0.8s" /> One was a drummer who talked a great deal and rapidly, three were Texans who did not care to talk, and two were quiet Mexican sheep herders. <break time="0.8s" /> Suddenly a young man appeared at the open door and cried that Scratchy Wilson was drunk and had turned loose with both hands. <break time="0.8s" /> The two Mexicans at once set down their glasses and faded out by the rear entrance, while the bartender quickly closed and barred the heavy doors. <break time="0.8s" /> The puzzled drummer asked whether there would be a fight, and one man answered grimly that he did not know about a fight, but there would be some shooting. <break time="0.8s" /> The men explained that Scratchy was the last of the old gang that used to hang out along the river, and that he was a terror when drunk. <break time="0.8s" /> When he was sober, he was the nicest fellow in town and would not hurt a fly, but drink turned him into a wild and dangerous man. <break time="0.8s" /> Only Jack Potter, the town marshal, had ever been able to handle him, and Potter, as everyone knew, was away in San Antonio.
